title: STE Line Studio
classification: Original illustrative interaction patterns, not observed systems or quantitative data

figures.title: Keep the evidence in reach.
figures.summary: A stack of source notes. Select a note to inspect its role. Heights and spacing are illustrative, not confidence or importance scores.

items.label: Original note
items.detail: Keep the unmodified material beside the explanation.

items.label: Observation
items.detail: State what was seen without adding a cause.

items.label: Qualification
items.detail: Retain scope, uncertainty, and contrary evidence.

items.label: Next question
items.detail: Identify what the source does not yet establish.

figures.title: Explore a neighborhood.
figures.summary: A proximity field responds to the pointer. The columns are an interaction metaphor, not measured values or inferred relationships.

items.label: Question
items.detail: Start with a specific reader question.

items.label: Source
items.detail: Inspect the material that can answer it.

items.label: Context
items.detail: Keep the surrounding conditions visible.

items.label: Comparison
items.detail: Choose a baseline that preserves meaning.

items.label: Limit
items.detail: Name what the evidence does not cover.

items.label: Revision
items.detail: Change the explanation when the source changes.

figures.title: Separate claims from presentation.
figures.summary: An exploded review stack. Layers describe responsibilities, not a real system architecture or a processing timeline.

items.label: Source
items.detail: Preserve the original input.

items.label: Claim
items.detail: Distinguish observation, attribution, inference, and proposal.

items.label: Explanation
items.detail: Choose the smallest useful medium.

items.label: Review
items.detail: Inspect both the evidence and the actual artifact.

figures.title: Trace a thought.
figures.summary: An editable pointer trail with a bounded history. The trace is a drawing, not telemetry, a waveform, or a measured event.

items.label: Begin
items.detail: Introduce a concrete example.

items.label: Connect
items.detail: Show the intermediate relationship.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Ask what the reader can now explain.

figures.title: Change your point of view.
figures.summary: Rotate the same three responsibilities. Camera angle changes the presentation, not the underlying evidence.

items.label: Author
items.detail: Makes the explanation clear.

items.label: Reader
items.detail: Needs a question answered.

items.label: Reviewer
items.detail: Checks claims and behavior independently.

figures.title: Follow the handoff.
figures.summary: A user-started pulse marks a conceptual handoff. Its speed is explanatory pacing, not latency or throughput.

items.label: Read
items.detail: Understand the supplied source.

items.label: Explain
items.detail: Write and visualize only what it supports.

items.label: Inspect
items.detail: Check the resulting artifact.

items.label: Deliver
items.detail: Return the useful result with material limits.
